ask: prune and minPres should both be synonyms of minimalPresentation.
note: met in substance. minPres === minimalPresentation is true, a real alias declared at m2/exports.m2:1308. prune is a separate method function -- m2/methods.m2:322 and :326 declare the two independently -- so prune === minimalPresentation is false, but they behave as synonyms: an identical set of all nine methods (CoherentSheaf, Complex, ComplexMap, Ideal, Matrix, Module, Ring, SheafMap, SheafOfRings), prune's doc body is empty with every way-to-use redirecting to the matching minimalPresentation node, and both are documented in minimalPresentation-doc.m2. Only object identity differs, with no user-visible consequence I could find. Correcting my earlier note on this row, which called the ask met because prune N == minimalPresentation N: that is equality of results on one module, not synonymy, so the old note was right by accident. Note the related #4504, open, proposing minimalPresentation be renamed minimizePresentation, which would revisit this naming anyway.

ask: minPres still needs to have how it deals with monomial orders repaired.
note: stands, and it is a silent wrong answer. Over R = QQ[a,b,c,d,MonomialOrder=>Lex] and S = R/ideal(a-b^2, c-d^3), minimalPresentation S returns a ring whose order is {MonomialSize=>32, Lex=>0, Position=>Up, GRevLex=>{1,1}} where two variables survive and it should be Lex=>2: the Lex block is emptied and a GRevLex block appended, and the GRevLex block is what orders the ring. Demonstrated rather than inferred -- leadTerm(b+d^3) is d^3 in the presentation against b in a genuine QQ[b,d,MonomialOrder=>Lex], since Lex takes the earlier variable and GRevLex the higher degree. prune is affected identically, sharing all nine methods and producing an order === to minimalPresentation's, and since prune is the commoner spelling that is how anyone will meet it. Narrow: surveyed six orders and only a Lex block spanning every variable fails. Default GRevLex gives GRevLex=>{1,1}, product {2,2} gives two GRevLex=>{1} blocks, Weights=>{1,2,3,4} correctly restricts to Weights=>{2,4}, Eliminate 2 gives Weights=>{1} which pads to eliminating b and keeping d as selectInSubring 1 confirms, and {Lex=>2,GRevLex=>2} correctly gives {Lex=>1,GRevLex=>{1}} -- so a Lex block inside a product order is fine. Cause region, not a traced line: monOrder at m2/minPres.m2:55 opens with if (Ord === Lex or Ord === GRevLex or Ord === RevLex), which cannot succeed now that MonomialOrder is a list rather than a bare symbol, so every order takes the branch written for product orders; that branch happens to be right for most shapes and wrong for this one. Two false leads I chased and discarded: I first blamed bare-count blocks generally, which {Lex=>2,GRevLex=>2} disproves, and an error I saw on the Eliminate presentation turned out to be my own script reusing variable names across two rings, not a defect. Complementary to #4621, which I filed earlier in this triage: that is the engine dropping an empty ordering block, this is minPres generating one, and fixing #4621 alone would leave the ring ordered by the spurious GRevLex block. Searched titles for minimalPresentation, minPres and monomial order, bodies for monOrder, minPres and MonomialOrder, and comments for minimalPresentation monomial, monOrder and minPres: #346 and its duplicate #347 are minPres raising 'key not found in hash table' on huge coefficients and #196 is prune ideal R erroring, all closed and none about orders.

ask: In documentation to minimalPrimes, finish example on absolute decomposition by showing how factor works over extension fields. Do the relevant interface to libfac first.
note: stands, and its stated prerequisite is already met. The doc node it names is packages/MinimalPrimes/doc.m2:126-131, which says the ideal 'is decomposed over the given field of coefficients and not over the extension field where the decomposition into absolutely irreducible factors occurs', shows minimalPrimes ideal(x^2+y^2) over QQ[w,x,y,z], and stops there -- so the reader is told what does not happen and never shown what does. That is exactly the unfinished example. The prerequisite, 'do the relevant interface to libfac first', is done: factor splits x^2+y^2 over an extension today, giving (x-i*y)*(x+i*y) over toField(QQ[i]/(i^2+1)), (x+(a+1)*y)*(x+(-a-1)*y) over GF 9, and factoring x^2-2 over GF(5,2). Two details the example ought to carry, both found while checking. toField is required -- over QQ[i]/(i^2+1) without it, factor returns x^2+y^2 unchanged, silently, which is a trap worth showing. And the finished example can only use factor and not minimalPrimes, because minimalPrimes over that extension raises 'no applicable strategy for (minimalPrimes,Ideal)' at MinimalPrimes.m2:239, which is documented behaviour -- the same node restricts the base ring to QQ or ZZ/p -- and is presumably why Dan wrote 'showing how factor works'. So this is one ask, a documentation completion, not two. Searched titles for absolute and minimalPrimes and bodies for 'absolutely irreducible': nothing covers it. #1017, radical over Galois fields, and #2839, a decompose and radical correctness bug, are the nearest and neither is this.

ask: Implement faster algorithms for radical: Krick/Logar in characteristic zero and Kemper in characteristic p>0. Rewrite documentation accordingly.
note: stands, and the source corroborates it. radical registers four strategies at packages/MinimalPrimes/radical.m2:129 -- Unmixed, Decompose, CompleteIntersection and Monomial -- and neither algorithm Dan names is among them; Krick, Logar and Kemper appear nowhere in the tree in this sense, the only Logar hits being Noether normalization and Quillen-Suslin. What the four are: Unmixed is unmixedradical or radical1, Decompose is intersect minimalPrimes, CompleteIntersection is an Eisenbud-Huneke-Vasconcelos method needing a complete intersection supplied, and Monomial defers to rawRadical. The header above them says the whole thing is 'Based on the Macaulay (classic) scripts written by D. Eisenbud. Translated from Macaulay to Macaulay2 by M. Stillman', so the core is still the classic translation. Stronger corroboration sits inside radical00 at radical.m2:57-60, which computes the separable part variable by variable under a comment reading 'there are THREE problems here! (a) use linear algebra (b) char p (c) f might not be the smallest eqn in var v_i' -- so the characteristic-p gap Kemper's algorithm addresses is acknowledged in the code itself, not just in this wishlist. Searched titles for radical, Krick and Kemper and bodies for Krick, Kemper and 'radical algorithm': nothing names either algorithm. #1017 (radical over Galois fields) and #2839 (a correctness bug in decompose and radical) are both open and both about correctness rather than speed. Searched more widely on Doug's instruction, since my first pass only grepped *.m2 under M2/Macaulay2: the author names appear nowhere in the tree in any file type, including undistributed-packages and the engine, the only Logar hits being NoetherNormalization and QuillenSuslin's Logar-Sturmfels, and the rest logarithm, logarg and dilogarithm. MinimalPrimes/radical.m2 is the only radical implementation; the engine's rawRadicalMonomialIdeal is monomial-only; Msolve mentions radicals only in a doc sentence about its input; GeometricDecomposability consumes radical(Unmixed=>true) rather than providing one. Filed without a benchmark, which the issue says plainly.

ask: Tor should allow noncommutative rings (exterior algebra)
note: duplicate of #150, which reframes it. stands, and the current state is finer than the ask. Over an exterior algebra E = QQ[e_1,e_2,e_3, SkewCommutative=>true], Tor_1 of two cyclic modules raises "'Tor' not implemented yet for noncommutative rings." from Complexes/Tor.m2:8. The same guard sits at Tor.m2:28 and, for Ext, at Complexes/ChainComplex.m2:1189 and ChainComplexMap.m2:719 and :738 -- five sites, one message. Hom carries no such guard and does work: Hom(E^1/ideal e_1, E^1/ideal e_2) returns subquotient(matrix{{e_1}}, matrix{{e_2}}). So of the three functors a reader would reach for, one works and two refuse. Somebody wanted this recently: #4459, 'Compute Hom and Ext over SkewCommutative rings', was opened June 2026 and is CLOSED UNMERGED -- its own body opens 'NOT READY FOR REVIEW AT ALL' and it depended on #4435 and #4176 -- so the attempt lapsed rather than landing. Searched titles for noncommutative, 'exterior algebra', skew and SkewCommutative, and bodies for 'Tor over noncommutative' and 'not implemented yet for noncommutative'; #2810 (Koszul differentials not compatible with exterior algebras), #3123 (tower of exterior algebras has incorrect multiplication) and #2783 (singularLocus for noncommutative inputs) are the neighbours and none is this. Doug asked whether I had checked comments, and I had not -- only titles and bodies. Searching comments turned up #150, 'dual modules over non-commutative rings', open since 2014, which says that over a noncommutative ring Hom(M,N) should not be an R-module, that Hom(M,R^1) can be a right module only if R carries an antiautomorphism, that 'there currently is no provision for that', and that consequently over an exterior algebra the dual of a chain complex fails to be a chain complex. That inverts the reading: the Ext and Tor guards may be deliberate and correct, and it is Hom going through unguarded that is anomalous. My drafted issue framed the guards as an oversight and would have been misleading, so it was withdrawn on Doug's call in favour of a comment on #150 carrying the user-visible symptoms -- the five guard sites, Hom's lack of one, and the lapsed #4459.

ask: quotient should check to see if the second arg is a variable -- in this case it should always use the "linear" strategy. [Merged with Dan's fourth paragraph: "time quotient(i3,S_0,Strategy=>Linear) Claims that the strategy is not implemented."]
note: stands, and Dan's two paragraphs are one piece of work, which is why they are merged here. Saturation.m2:241 defines a Linear strategy for quotient that is a stub: it checks that the input is homogeneous and that isLinearForm J_0, then prints 'warning: quotient strategy Linear is not yet implemented' and returns null. So the auto-select precondition Dan asks for in his second paragraph is already written, inside the strategy his fourth paragraph reports as unimplemented -- the two are halves of one unfinished feature, and filing them apart would leave an issue that cannot be acted on until its sibling is done. Doug agreed to merge. The strategy is worse off than the stub suggests: Linear is commented out of the hook registration itself at Saturation.m2:261, scan({Quotient, Iterate-* Linear *-, Monomial}, ...), and likewise for (quotient, Module, Ideal) at :306, so a caller never reaches the warning and instead gets 'unrecognized Strategy => Linear for (quotient,Ideal,Ideal)'. Checked and did not overstate: Linear is not advertised anywhere in the documentation -- the [quotient, Strategy] node at Saturation/quotient-doc.m2:97 describes Quotient and Iterate and directs the reader to hooks for the list -- so this is an unimplemented internal strategy rather than a broken published promise. The default path is unaffected and correct: quotient(I, ideal x) and I : x agree. Searched titles for quotient and 'Linear strategy' and bodies for 'quotient strategy Linear': nothing covers it. Comments searched too, on Doug's prompt: #1317 (closed, 2020) quotes help advertising 'Possible strategies are: Iterate, Linear, and Quotient', which would have made Linear a broken published promise -- but that enumeration is gone today, so the feature-request framing stands rather than a bug. Nothing else in comments touches it.

ask: minimal resolutions over local rings.
note: met. The LocalRings package registers a freeResolution hook at LocalRings.m2:325-334 with Strategy => Local which lifts the module up to the polynomial ring with liftUp, resolves it there, tensors the result back with R_P, and then prunes -- pruneComplex(CP, UnitTest => isScalar, PruningMap => false) when the lifted module is homogeneous, plain pruneComplex otherwise. Pruning is what delivers minimality, and the package header states that as the design: 'The main lemma involves lifting the objects from R_P back to R, performing the operation, then localizing by tensoring with R_P and pruning the resolution.' Verified on RP = localRing(QQ[a,b,c], ideal(a,b,c)) and M = RP^1/(ideal(a^2,a*b)): res M gives ranks {1,2,1} with differentials {{a^2, a*b}} and {{-b},{a}}, every entry in the maximal ideal, so that resolution is minimal. Two false trails worth recording so they are not re-walked. LocalRings/examples.m2:226 carries '--Not necessarily minimal!!' and :240 'pruneComplex C -- just to make sure it's minimal', which look like the package disclaiming minimality; neither does. The first is about pruneComplex with a custom UnitTest over a polynomial ring, and the second resolves an ideal of R rather than of RP, so it never reaches the local hook. And my first minimality check failed with 'GB computation for non-polynomial rings not yet re-implemented' -- a real further gap in local ring support, but not one Dan asked about -- so minimality was established by inspecting the differentials instead.

ask: hilbertFunction applied to a CoherentSheaf doesn't work as desired. It needs to be fixed. At the moment the relevant page is commented out of the documentation.
note: resolved by deciding against it rather than by fixing it, and the mathematics explains why. There is no (hilbertFunction, ZZ, CoherentSheaf) method today -- methods hilbertFunction lists only Ring, Module and Ideal against ZZ or List -- and no commented-out sheaf page survives in hilbertFunction-doc.m2. The obstruction is real: a Hilbert function counts graded pieces of a module, and a sheaf does not determine them, since two modules with the same sheafification differ in low degrees exactly when one is unsaturated. What is well defined for a sheaf is provided: (hilbertPolynomial, CoherentSheaf) and (euler, CoherentSheaf) both exist. So 'doesn't work as desired' was a symptom of asking a module question of a sheaf, and the resolution was to offer the sheaf-invariant notions instead. See [[bugs/dan/0-bugs-lgold.m2::3]] and ::5, which are the same obstruction from two other directions.

ask: Also hilbertSeries applied to a CoherentSheaf doesn't work as desired. It needs to be fixed. At the moment the relevant page is commented out of the documentation.
note: same resolution as ::2 and for the same reason. methods hilbertSeries lists ZZ with BettiTally, PolynomialRing, QuotientRing, Ideal, Module and ProjectiveHilbertPolynomial -- no CoherentSheaf -- and hilbertSeries-doc.m2 carries no commented-out sheaf page. A Hilbert series is a generating function for the dimensions of a module's graded pieces, so it is not a sheaf invariant; only its eventual behaviour, captured by the Hilbert polynomial, is, and (hilbertPolynomial, CoherentSheaf) exists. Verified that hilbertSeries of a sheaf raises no method found rather than returning something wrong.

ask: Check that the saturation is being used for hilbertSeries of a ProjectiveVariety.
note: moot: there is no (hilbertSeries, ProjectiveVariety) method to check. Confirmed by running it -- hilbertSeries Proj(R/I) raises 'no method found for applying hilbertSeries to ... of class ProjectiveVariety' -- and by methods hilbertSeries, which lists no variety or sheaf. This is the same obstruction as ::2 and ::3: giving a variety a Hilbert series would require saturating first, since the series depends on the module and not the scheme, which is presumably the concern behind the ask. M2's resolution was to provide only the saturation-independent invariants, (hilbertPolynomial, ProjectiveVariety) and (euler, ProjectiveVariety). Checked that this really is independent rather than quietly saturating: on I = ideal(a^2,a*b,a*c) whose saturation is ideal a, hilbertPolynomial agrees with hilbertPolynomial of the saturated variety, {1 => 1} both ways, and euler is 2 both ways -- and the module-level hilbertPolynomial agrees too, which shows the agreement is the Hilbert polynomial's insensitivity to saturation rather than a saturation step being applied.

ask: Would like a better example for PoincareN where there are different steps of the resolution which have the same degree.
note: met, and the existing example has exactly the property asked for. The function moved and was renamed: PoincareN is now poincareN in the Complexes package, implemented at Complexes/ChainComplex.m2:670 and documented at ChainComplexDoc.m2:4261 onwards, which Macaulay2Doc's hilbertSeries and hilbertPolynomial pages cross-reference as 'Complexes :: poincareN'. Its second example is C = freeResolution ideal(a*b, b*c*d, c*d*e^2) over ZZ/32003[a..f], and running it gives poincareN C = 1+S*T_0^2+S*T_0^3+S*T_0^4+S^2*T_0^4+S^2*T_0^5. T_0^4 appears with both S and S^2, so two different homological steps share an internal degree, which is precisely the case the file wanted illustrated -- and it is the case that shows why poincareN needs a separate variable for homological degree at all. The betti table confirms the overlap, columns 1 and 2 both having entries in rows 2 and 3.

ask: There should exist a command like faceRing SimplicialComplex which returns the Stanley Reisner ring; currently this works with StanleyReisnerRing.facering but it is not exported. Fix also documentation for dim accordingly.
note: declined by a rewrite rather than left undone, and the documentation half needs nothing. ask: Why does there exist (codim, PolynomialRing)??
note: a question rather than a request, and it has a good answer, so nothing needs changing. m2/monideal.m2:102 defines codim PolynomialRing := ... -> 0 immediately above codim QuotientRing := ... -> codim(cokernel presentation R, opts) at :103. The pair makes codim total on rings: a polynomial ring is its own ambient ring, so its codimension there is 0, and the two lines together let codim be applied uniformly whether or not a ring is a quotient. m2/quotring.m2:296 relies on exactly that, calling codim(R, Generic => true) without knowing which kind of ring R is. Verified that codim QQ[x,y,z] returns 0. Searched titles for codim: the one open hit, #3557 on rank failing over ZZ for want of Generic => true, is unrelated.

ask: M2 yields zero and not the expected result for nonfreelocus = sheafExt^2(FF, OO_projplane^1), where projplane = Proj(ZZ/101[a,b,c]) and FF = sheaf(kernel(matrix{{1,1,1}}*koszul(2,vars R))).
note: not a bug: zero is the correct answer, and the expectation behind the variable name is what is mistaken. The sheaf is locally free, so it has no non-free locus for sheafExt to detect. Worked out rather than assumed: koszul(2,vars R) is matrix {{-b,-c,0},{a,0,-c},{0,a,b}}, so matrix{{1,1,1}}*koszul(2,vars R) is the 1x3 matrix {{a-b, a-c, b-c}}, and prune of its kernel is a free module -- isFreeModule returns true with degrees {{1},{2}} and betti res showing two generators in degrees 1 and 2. Hence FF is OO(-1) ++ OO(-2), and sheafExt^i(FF, OO) vanishes for i >= 1 as it must for a sum of line bundles. Consistent with the reporter's own rank FF of 2, and with sheafExt^0(FF, OO) returning OO(1) ++ OO(2), the dual. Confirmed M2 is not simply returning zero always: on P^1, sheafExt^1(sheaf coker matrix{{x,y}}, OO) returns a nonzero subquotient. ask: consider exporting function warningMessage and documenting it
note: stands, and it is the other half of ask 3. warningMessage is defined at m2/debugging.m2:17 and is not in m2/exports.m2, so package authors cannot reach it. What it does is not merely printing: warningMessage0 hashes the message, emits 'warning: <args>' to stderr, and then tells the reader how to turn that specific warning into an error -- 'debug with expression debug <h> or with command line option --debug <h>'. That hashcode is exactly what --debug n consumes, so ask 3 documents the consumer of a producer that ask 4 asks to be made public. printerr is exported (m2/exports.m2:1036) and documented, but it is only stderr << commentize msg << endl: no warning: prefix, no hashcode, no participation in the debug mechanism. So a package author today can print a message but cannot raise a warning a user can convert into an error. Dan wrote 'consider exporting', which is a suggestion rather than a demand, and that is worth carrying into however this is reported. Searched titles, bodies and comments for warningMessage: nothing anywhere, so it is untracked. Duplicate of #2582 rather than filed, per Doug's call, with a comment there cross-referencing #540 and #2771. Doug asked what --debug even does, being a core developer who did not know, and digging changed the outcome twice. What it does: warningMessage0 hashes the formatted message to (hash args) % 10000, prints it, and if debugWarningHashcode matches raises an error instead -- verified both ways, converting at debugging.m2:10 when set beforehand. Three flaws found. The code names the message text and not the warning site, so package XML gives 1900, Foo 7501 and Depth 160 for one warning, and rewording moves it, 7615 to 352; nothing can be documented. It collides -- 10000 buckets, and that one warning over the 299 installed packages yields five genuine collisions, TropicalToric with Resultants at 534 among them. And half its own advice is unusable: debug n typed afterwards cannot catch a state-changing warning, since the state has already changed and it cannot recur, which is exactly why #2582's author got nothing from debug 2671. Then the duplicate search, which I had not done for this claim until asked: #2582 is a direct report of that third flaw, open since 2022, and #540 and #2771 both quote the same debug line as part of what makes these warnings look like bugs. So a new issue would have duplicated #2582. Practical context in the comment: 14 packages hand-roll warning text, 0 use warningMessage, and Schubert2.m2:486 rewords Core's variables.m2:21 message because it cannot call it.

ask: Interrupt handling might work better if the interpreter were all compiled in C++ and used C++ exceptions, but how do we make that work with multiple threads?
note: not filable: a speculation carrying its own unresolved objection, and both halves check out as partly-underway rather than neglected. The C++ half is real and in progress: d/Makefile.in:48-52 defines choice2 = all: $(patsubst %.d,%$(1),$(patsubst %.dd,%$(2),$(3))) and invokes it as $(call choice2,-tmp.c,-tmp.cc,$d), so .d compiles as C and .dd as C++, and of 68 sources 18 are already .dd -- actors2 boostmath buckets chrono classes debugging engine equality hashtables interface interp monoid monomial_ordering profiler regex sets threads version. interp.dd is among them, so the interpreter core Dan wanted moved is across already; 50 .d files are not, confirmed against a build tree carrying 49 -tmp.c and 18 -tmp.cc. Nobody needs an issue to keep converting files one at a time. The exceptions half is not done: interrupt handling is still flag-based, d/interp.dd:95 reading interruptPending = false; determineExceptionFlag(), so moving a file to C++ has not by itself changed the mechanism. Dan's objection is live rather than hypothetical, since threads.dd and system/supervisor.cpp both exist now. Tested whether the flag mechanism is a common cause behind the open interrupt bugs, which would have given the speculation practical weight: it is not. #3885 is Normaliz, an external library taking the signal, where unwinding in the interpreter cannot help; #4144 is a feature request for the Ctrl-C prompt; #4567 is run's signal forwarding against its documentation, which I filed earlier in this triage; only #3856 is adjacent and that is freeResolution's cached LengthLimit surviving an interrupt, a cache rather than stack unwinding. So there is no evidence exceptions would fix anything now open, which is what would have made this actionable. Searched titles for interrupt, C++, exception, scc1 and thread; bodies for 'C++ exceptions', .dd and scc1; comments for 'C++ exceptions', 'interpreter in C++', 'scc1 C++' and 'interrupt handling'. Nothing tracks either half: #985 is modernising the engine's C++, not the interpreter, #2247 is documentation for the interpreter, #4562 and #1197 are scc1 defects (an assertion on string.d, and #ifdef support), #4495 is the non-ANSI attribute in generated C that I filed earlier here, and #4321 is cmake on macOS.
